paragraphs.text: A [red tea](red:definition) from Taiwan, made in 2023. It is the fully oxidised style English calls black tea: the leaf is withered, rolled so its juices and enzymes meet, then left to [oxidise](red:making) until it turns from green to reddish brown, and dried to stop the change. The island’s own red tea dates from the [Japanese period](red:history), at Yuchi near Sun Moon Lake.

Red tea has no tradition of [ageing](red:ageing). Sealed, it keeps its quality for about a year and a half to three years, so at three years this one sits at the far end of that span. It is a tea to drink now, not to set aside.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
